items.confirmed_defect: F1 identifies arbitrary star-homomorphisms with bounded ones although the definition specifies bounded star-homomorphisms separately; proof 1.3 uses a bound M and only proves bounded-map contractivity.

exact_edits.text: [F1] $A$ and $B$ are C\*-algebras with $\|a^*a\|=\|a\|^2$; when $A$ is nonunital, $A^+$ is a unital C\*-algebra containing $A$ as a closed two-sided $\ast$-ideal of codimension one and its norm extends the norm of $A$. Here an algebraic star-homomorphism means a complex-linear map preserving products and the involution, with no continuity or unitality assumed; bounded star-homomorphisms are defined separately. The algebraic unitization has product $(a,\lambda)(b,\mu)=(ab+\lambda b+\mu a,\lambda\mu)$ and involution $(a,\lambda)^*=(a^*,\overline\lambda)$ ([[def-c-star-algebra]], [[thm-minimal-c-star-unitization]], [[def-algebraic-unitization-of-a-star-algebra]], [[def-unital-banach-algebra]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-elements-of-a-c-star-algebra]]).

1.3 Let $\varphi:E\to F$ be an algebraic star-homomorphism of C\*-algebras. Give the forced algebraic unitizations $E^\dagger=E\oplus\mathbb C$ and $F^\dagger=F\oplus\mathbb C$ C\*-norms extending the original norms: for genuinely nonunital algebras use [F1], including its zero case, and for a unital algebra $E$ use the algebraic $\ast$-isomorphism $(a,\lambda)\mapsto(a+\lambda1_E,\lambda)$ onto $E\times\mathbb C$ with norm $\max(\|a+\lambda1_E\|,|\lambda|)$; coordinatewise completeness, submultiplicativity and the C\*-identity verify this norm, and $(a,0)$ has norm $\|a\|$. The map $\varphi^\dagger(a,\lambda)=(\varphi(a),\lambda)$ is an algebraic unital $\ast$-homomorphism by the unitization formulas. If $z-\lambda1$ is invertible, $\varphi^\dagger((z-\lambda1)^{-1})$ is the inverse of $\varphi^\dagger(z)-\lambda1$, so $\sigma_{F^\dagger}(\varphi^\dagger(z))\subseteq\sigma_{E^\dagger}(z)$. Apply this to the self-adjoint element $z=(a^*a,0)$ and use [F4] in both unital C\*-algebras to obtain $\|\varphi(a)\|^2=\|\varphi(a^*a)\|=r_{F^\dagger}(\varphi^\dagger(z))\le r_{E^\dagger}(z)=\|a^*a\|=\|a\|^2$. Thus every algebraic star-homomorphism is contractive, and in particular continuous. [F1, F4, algebra]

exact_edits.text: [F2] For $T_g=WU_gW^{-1}$ and the canonical scalar translation $V_g$, the operators $W_g=V_g^{-1}T_g$ are multiplication by jointly Borel, a.e. unitary fields $\varphi_g$, with $\varphi_{g_1g_2}(x)=\varphi_{g_1}(g_2x)\varphi_{g_2}(x)$ for each pair and almost every $x$ ([[lem-borel-cocycle-fields-for-imprimitivity-systems]]).

[F3] If the fields of [F2] are continuous in local measure in the strong topology, Haar regularization gives a Borel unitary field $B$ and a strongly continuous unitary $\sigma:H\to U(K)$ with $\varphi_g(x)=B(gx)\sigma(s(gx)^{-1}gs(x))B(x)^{-1}$ for every $g$ and almost every $x$. The formula defines a strict Borel cocycle, and $\sigma$ is unique up to unitary equivalence ([[lem-haar-regularization-of-transitive-unitary-cocycles]], [[lem-borel-cross-sections-for-closed-subgroups]]).

[F8] The finite quasi-invariant $\mu$ is equivalent to a rho-derived Radon measure $\nu$; a positive finite Borel version of $a=d\mu/d\nu$ exists, and scalar unitary induction is strongly continuous. Borel homomorphisms $H\to U(K)$ are strongly continuous when $K$ is separable ([[lem-haar-lifts-and-borel-descent-on-a-homogeneous-space]], [[thm-radon-nikodym-density-exists-and-is-unique-up-to-almost-everywhere-equality]], [[thm-unitary-induction-from-a-closed-subgroup]], [[lem-steinhaus-and-pettis-for-second-countable-locally-compact-groups]]).

exact_edits.text:
1.2 Apply [F1] to obtain $W,\mu,K$ and put $T_g=WU_gW^{-1}$; [F2] gives the Borel source-variable cocycle fields. Choose $
u$ and $a=d\mu/d
u$ from [F8] and set $Jf=\sqrt a\,f$. Then $J:L^2(\mu;K)	o L^2(
u;K)$ is unitary. Pushing the equality $d\mu=a\,d
u$ through the base translation gives $D_g^\mu(x)=a(g^{-1}x)a(x)^{-1}D_g^
u(x)$ almost everywhere, so $JV_g^\mu J^{-1}=V_g^
u$. The scalar $V_g^
u$ is induction of the trivial representation of $H$ and is strongly continuous by [F8]; this extends to $K$-valued sections first on finite sums $f(x)\xi$ and then by their density and unitarity. Hence $V_g^\mu$ is strongly continuous. Since $T_g$ is strongly continuous, so is $W_g=(V_g^\mu)^{-1}T_g$, by the triangle inequality and unitary norm bounds. [F1, F2, F8, given]

1.3 Fix $g_0\in G$, a Borel $E\subseteq G/H$ with $\mu(E)<\infty$, and $\xi\in K$. Since $\mathbf1_E\xi\in L^2(\mu;K)$ and $W_g=M_{\varphi_g}$, step 1.2 gives $\int_E\|(\varphi_g(x)-\varphi_{g_0}(x))\xi\|^2\,d\mu(x)=\|(W_g-W_{g_0})(\mathbf1_E\xi)\|_2^2	o0$. Therefore $\mu\{x\in E:\|(\varphi_g(x)-\varphi_{g_0}(x))\xi\|>\varepsilon\}\le\varepsilon^{-2}\|(W_g-W_{g_0})(\mathbf1_E\xi)\|_2^2	o0$. On the unitary group, the strong topology is determined by a countable dense set of vectors in separable $K$: finite-vector tests pass to every vector using $\|(u-v)(\xi-\eta)\|\le2\|\xi-\eta\|$. Finite unions of the displayed exceptional sets thus prove local convergence in measure in the strong topology. This is the continuity hypothesis required in [F3]. [F2, F7, step 1.2, algebra]

1.4 Now [F3] applies with its continuity hypothesis verified by step 1.3 and supplies $B,\sigma$. In the Haar proof the lifted coboundary $b$ has $b(th)=b(t)\sigma(h)$ for each $h$ and almost every $t$. Thus $\sigma(hk)=\sigma(h)\sigma(k)$; integrating the Borel matrix coefficients of $b(t)^{-1}b(th)$ against a fixed Haar probability density makes every coefficient of $\sigma$ Borel. Since $K$ is separable, [F8] applies to this Borel homomorphism and gives strong continuity. Invariant Borel descent of $b(s(x)h)\sigma(h)^{-1}$ gives $B(x)$, and the resulting section-cocycle formula is strict on all pairs after replacing the fields by their equal a.e. representatives. [F3, F8, step 1.3]

1.5 Multiplication by the Borel unitaries $B(x)$ is unitary and commutes with indicator multiplications. Put $\Phi=M_B^{-1}W$. Substituting the factorization from step 1.4 at the source point $g^{-1}x$ gives $(\Phi U_g\Phi^{-1}f)(x)=D_g^\mu(x)^{1/2}\sigma(s(x)^{-1}gs(g^{-1}x))f(g^{-1}x)$ and $\Phi P(E)\Phi^{-1}=M_{\mathbf1_E}$. This is the section-coordinate form of the canonical induced action, as in [F4], so $\Phi$ is the required unitary and may be denoted $W$ in the statement. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.4]

1.7 Start with the canonical system of $\sigma$. Its source-variable cocycle is $\varphi_g(x)=\sigma(s(gx)^{-1}gs(x))$, so $(B,\sigma)=(I,\sigma)$ is already a factorization. Any recovered representation $\sigma'$ is unitarily equivalent to $\sigma$ by the uniqueness clause of [F3]. Conversely step 1.5 reconstructs a system unitarily equivalent to the starting $(U,P)$. Thus the constructions are inverse up to unitary equivalence. [F3, F5, step 1.5]

2.1 Steps 1.2–1.5 prove the forward direction, including the local-measure continuity and strongly continuous stabilizer action; steps 1.6 and 1.7 give the converse and inverse character up to unitary equivalence. The zero case is covered by step 1.1. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, step 1.4, step 1.5, step 1.6, step 1.7, F7] ∎

prerequisite_checks: Cocycle supplier Statement supplies Borel representatives, a.e. unitarity for every fixed g, and pairwise a.e. cocycle identity; continuity is not treated as a supplied fact.
Haar-lift Statement supplies equivalence of finite quasi-invariant mu with a rho-derived Radon nu, product/Haar null-class equivalence and Borel invariant descent.

Scalar induction strong continuity comes from thm-unitary-induction-from-a-closed-subgroup with trivial one-dimensional H-representation; its published dependency proof supplies strong continuity without Mackey. Density and finite tensor sums extend this to K-valued scalar translations.

RN theorem supplies a=dmu/dnu positive finite a.e. (sigma-finite measures); the explicit change-of-measure computation proves conjugacy, avoiding inappropriate use of the equivalent-Radon theorem when finite mu need not be Radon.

Haar regularization Statement has precisely the Borel, pairwise a.e. cocycle, separability, homogeneous-space class and local-measure continuity hypotheses. The newly proved estimate verifies its missing hypothesis.

Read full local Haar proof 1.1–8.1: Fubini lift C(u,v)=c(uv^-1,q(v)), b coboundary for almost all g; continuity upgrades to every g; right-H ratios are constants; coefficient integration makes sigma Borel; Pettis makes it continuous; invariant Borel descent gives B; uniqueness follows from constant ratio of lifted trivializations.

Read full Pettis proof: finite positive Haar set A gives AA^-1 identity neighborhood by L2 translation continuity; countable target cover gives positive measure preimage of a small neighborhood; Steinhaus gives continuity. U(K) is second countable for separable K, with multiplication and inversion SOT-continuous.

Haar proof fixed finite-measure sets beyond relatively compact sets can be handled by truncating to compacta: bounded unitary coefficients control the omitted measure. No obstruction found in the bounded pass.
